---
title: "Hackathon 1"
subtitle: "Bringing research tools to SURF Research Cloud"
---

A research tool is only as accessible as the effort it takes to get it running. Many tools only work on their developer's own machine or need a long, fragile installation. For other researchers, that is often enough reason not to try them at all.

[SURF Research Cloud](https://www.surf.nl/en/services/surf-research-cloud) offers a way around this. Researchers in the Netherlands can start a ready-to-use workspace with a tool already installed, without setting anything up themselves. Getting a tool onto the platform, however, takes some technical work that many research software developers have not done before.

This first of two hackathons, held on 2 February at the SURF office in Utrecht, brought developers together to do that work, with hands-on support. Participants worked on making their own tools available on SURF Research Cloud, so that other researchers can start using them with just a few clicks.

Developers of the following tools took part:

- [Mutalyzer](https://mutalyzer.nl)
- [Elastix](https://github.com/SuperElastix/elastix)
- [AOP-Wiki SNORQL](https://aopwiki.rdf.bigcat-bioinformatics.org/)
- [dnabarcoder](https://github.com/vuthuyduong/dnabarcoder)
- [WikiPathways](https://www.wikipathways.org) and [BridgeDb](https://www.bridgedb.org)
- [metataxonx-nf](https://github.com/CMG-GUTS/metataxonx)
- [SIQPlotteR](https://github.com/RobinVanSchendel/SIQ)
- [quickLD](https://github.com/pephco/quickLD) and [RAiSD-AI](https://github.com/alachins/RAiSD-AI)

The second hackathon continued this work; see [Hackathon 2](3hackathon2.qmd) for the progress made.
